finding.title: Split curriculum_label.dart (451 lines) and domain_term_labels.dart (435 lines) below the 400-line hand-written cap
finding.why: Both files exceed the 400-line hand-written Dart cap. curriculum_label.dart's bulk is largely 8 near-identical named constructors, each null-initializing the same 10 fields (~130 lines of pure boilerplate) — a tagged union modeled as one class with nullable fields instead of a sealed hierarchy, which is also the structural reason the ancestor-Hebrew-name plumbing (see the P1 finding) is easy to miss in one branch and not another. domain_term_labels.dart's bulk is the deliberate, documented per-curriculum siyum-label catalog (lines ~346-428). Long files raise review/merge-conflict cost and make it harder to hold one rendering mode's full context while editing.
finding.recommendation: For curriculum_label.dart: extract the per-mode constructors/build-cases into a sealed _CurriculumLabelData hierarchy (one variant class per _Kind) to remove the repeated null-field boilerplate. For domain_term_labels.dart: split the per-curriculum siyum catalog into a sibling file (e.g. curriculum_siyum_labels.dart) or mixin.
acceptance_criteria: AG-3 checker (once implemented per Rule 0) passes on lib/core/labels/**.

finding.title: Hoist the RegExp allocated on every call inside DomainTermLabels._normaliseEnglishStageName
finding.rule: PF-3 spirit (avoid per-call allocation on a list-render path); Fowler 'extract constant'
finding.why: _normaliseEnglishStageName is invoked from resolveStoredStageName, which (per its own doc comment and the PP-5 regression test) is called once per StageBreakdownEntry.stageName in list rendering — i.e. per row, potentially on every rebuild. Compiling a new RegExp on every call is needless allocation on a path this same file's sibling curriculum_label.dart already knows to avoid: its own Hebrew-detection pattern is hoisted to a static final (curriculum_label.dart:364, `static final RegExp _hebrew = RegExp(...)`).
finding.recommendation: Hoist to a private `static final RegExp _reviewNumbered = RegExp(r'^Review (\d+)$');` at class scope, mirroring curriculum_label.dart's _hebrew pattern.
acceptance_criteria: _normaliseEnglishStageName allocates no new RegExp per call — verified by code review or a grep for `RegExp(` inside method bodies (not field initializers) under lib/core/labels/.

finding.title: Delete dead core/navigation re-export shims and break the app_router↔guards import cycle
finding.rule: coding-standards.md:63 "dependency direction is strictly app → features → core"; adjacent to Rule 2's "do not add other barrel/re-export files"
finding.why: The W1.2 refactor (commit eb9e7fb7, message: "Old core/navigation/ paths become re-export stubs so all 42 importers keep compiling without mass edits") moved the real router files to lib/app/router/ but the promised cleanup never happened. Three of this batch's own guards (pin_guard.dart:3, profile_guard.dart:6, restore_guard.dart:8) still import the OLD core/navigation/app_router.dart shim to reach route classes, and lib/app/router/app_router.dart imports those same three guards (line 8 and neighbours) — producing a real import cycle app→core→(shim)→app that spans exactly the boundary coding-standards.md:63 calls "strict". Dart tolerates the cycle at compile time, but it makes the documented layering diagram false and blocks ever extracting core/ as a standalone package. Two of the four shims are worse than merely redundant: app_shell.dart has zero importers anywhere in the repo (fully dead), and guards/auth_guard.dart is imported only by 3 test files (test/core/navigation/app_shell_test.dart, auth_guard_test.dart, story_acceptance/epic_01_foundation_test.dart) — production code already migrated off it, tests didn't.
finding.recommendation: Point pin_guard.dart/profile_guard.dart/restore_guard.dart's route-class imports at lib/app/router/app_router.dart directly (or, better, pass the needed PageRouteInfo constructors in via the guard constructor so core/ guards don't need to know about app/router at all). Delete app_shell.dart outright (dead). Delete guards/auth_guard.dart and repoint its 3 remaining test importers at lib/app/router/guards/auth_guard.dart. Leave router_provider.dart's shim only if a follow-up ticket is filed to finish its migration too.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rln "core/navigation/app_shell.dart\|core/navigation/guards/auth_guard.dart" learning_tracker/lib learning_tracker/test` returns no matches (files deleted, callers repointed).
make audit gains a core→app check mirroring existing check 14/15 (core→features).

finding.title: Rename core/utils/date_utils.dart's DateUtils class off the Flutter SDK's own DateUtils name
finding.rule: AG-4 (public top-level symbol names unique across lib/)
finding.why: package:flutter/material.dart exports its own `abstract final class DateUtils` (src/material/date.dart:247, re-exported at material.dart:65) with methods like isSameDay/getDaysInMonth used elsewhere in this repo (e.g. monthly_activity_sliver_calendar.dart calls Flutter's DateUtils.getDaysInMonth). This project's core/utils/date_utils.dart declares a second, unrelated `class DateUtils` with different semantics (isSameLocalDay is deliberately UTC→local-day aware per the P5 streak-boundary pattern; Flutter's isSameDay is a raw field compare). At least 14 lib/ files and 25+ test files import both material.dart and this file unqualified; exactly one file (goal_setup_screen.dart:1) already needed `hide DateUtils` to compile because it calls the project's DateUtils.extractLocalDate. Any of the other ~39 files is one `DateUtils.` autocomplete away from either a hard "ambiguous import" compile error or — if an agent "fixes" it by hiding the wrong side — silently swapping in Flutter's timezone-naive comparison where the streak-safe local-day comparison was intended, a domain the whole file exists to get right.
finding.recommendation: Rename the project's class (e.g. LocalDayUtils) or fold its 4 static methods into DateTimeFactory in the same file, so it no longer shadows the Flutter SDK name. Remove goal_setup_screen.dart's now-unnecessary `hide DateUtils` after the rename.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "^class DateUtils" learning_tracker/lib/` returns no matches (class renamed).
goal_setup_screen.dart's `hide DateUtils` clause is removed and the file still compiles, confirming no remaining ambiguity.

finding.title: Rename the three core/utils/*_utils.dart files off the banned _utils.dart suffix

evidence.quote: /// Utilities for date handling following P5 pattern:
/// Hebrew calendar utilities wrapping kosher_dart library.

finding.why: `find lib -iname '*_utils.dart'` returns exactly these 3 files — 100% of the repo's occurrences of a naming pattern the standard bans by name. None is a sprawling god-file today (72-148 lines, single-topic), but the suffix itself is the violation, and a Rule-0 grep checker for this rule would fail on exactly these 3 files with no other candidates to triage.
finding.recommendation: Rename to role-specific names: hebrew_calendar_utils.dart → hebrew_calendar_service.dart; hebrew_utils.dart → sefaria_text_cleaner.dart (its only real job); date_utils.dart → split per the DateUtils-collision finding (DateTimeFactory folds into core/time/, the DateUtils class becomes local_day_math.dart).
acceptance_criteria: make/audit gains this as a grep check per AG-3's own pattern.
